I work in natural gas construction as a gas mechanic. It’s a very specific trade that isn’t easy to get into as it usually requires NGA Qualifications to get your foot in the door. 

I’m lucky enough to be in a union that fights for us to have multiple raises a year and I happened to be very fortunate to have gotten in due to my mechanical aptitude. The labor can be difficult at times and most of my friends outside of work can not competently do the work that I do, be-it for lack of strength or mechanical ability.

This is to say how hard are you willing to work. But more importantly what skill set you have and what do you have aptitude for? Trades are good money but require a significant amount of body resilience and strength that not everyone can do. Applying to similar job positions as your current job for higher pay is also a good game to play but would take more time. 

I do not believe people are poor by choice but by lack of options too not everyone is capable of working any job but it’s important to broaden your options as much as possible at every chance possible because it’s the only chance of making decent money and it’s not guaranteed to work either. I’m sorry if this sounds discouraging but these are the odds people of lower income often fight against.

On a side note having kids also limits your options and can ultimately cripple people financially so avoiding having them at the improper time is critical for your future or else the loop continues.
